tools.name: search
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to find, compare, or answer a question about current U.S. free trials, rebates, bonuses, cash back, or other actionable savings. It returns citable answer guides and normalized records. Fetch the best returned id before giving detailed terms. Do not use it for purchases,

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Use this after search returns a guide:SLUG, trial:SLUG, or entitlement:SLUG id and the user needs the complete answer, terms, evidence, verification state, or official action path. Do not guess ids, substitute a guide URL for an offer action, or use this for an id from another service.

tools.name: search_freebies
tools.description: Use this when the user needs explicit corpus scope, result limits, or a rich normalized list rather than the standard citable search/fetch flow. It is read-only: the default uses site-controlled actionable U.S. trials and savings, while only an explicit open-source scope reads public GitHub. Use pub

tools.name: get_record
tools.description: Use this after search_freebies returns an exact trial or entitlement id and the user needs its complete normalized terms, conditions, sources, official action path, or latest verification state. Do not guess ids or treat a directory-only or inconclusive record as confirmed.

tools.name: get_verification
tools.description: Use this when the user asks how or when one exact Andrew’s Freebies record was checked, whether its terms matched, or what audit warnings exist. Catalog status and audit outcome are separate; blocked, unknown, and fetch errors never prove expiration, and audits never remove or change records.

tools.name: get_freshness
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about catalog-wide verification freshness, overdue coverage, scheduler liveness, or records sharing an audit outcome. Do not use aggregate freshness to prove that one offer is active; inspect that record and its verification history instead. Blocked or unknown never means

tools.name: flag_expired_deal
tools.description: Use this only when the user supplies an exact existing record id and relevant current first-party evidence showing that its offer ended or is unavailable. findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.
